content.text: {"screening_id":"SCR_000012","question_assessments":[{"domain_id":"D1","question_id":"1.1","agent_response":"Y","evidence_location":"Page 3, Methods, “Randomization, Allocation Concealment, and Blinding”","evidence_summary":"Participants were assigned 1:1 using an automated REDCap system, with stratification by age and eGFR and variable block sizes.","rationale":"An automated system using variable-block, stratified randomization is an explicitly random sequence-generation method.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D1","question_id":"1.2","agent_response":"PY","evidence_location":"Page 3, Methods, “Randomization, Allocation Concealment, and Blinding”","evidence_summary":"Randomization and assignment were performed through an automated REDCap system. The report does not describe advance access to the allocation list or the exact assignment workflow.","rationale":"Automated system-based assignment probably prevented foreknowledge of allocation, although concealment until irrevocable enrollment is not described in full detail.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D1","question_id":"1.3","agent_response":"N","evidence_location":"Page 5, Table 1, baseline characteristics","evidence_summary":"Groups were broadly comparable in age, diabetes history, kidney function, HbA1c, coronary anatomy, and operative characteristics. Some differences, such as sex, ACE inhibitor/ARB use, and reduced ejection fraction, were modest and not consistently directional.","rationale":"The observed differences are compatible with chance in a trial of this size and do not provide persuasive evidence of a randomization failure.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.1","agent_response":"Y","evidence_location":"Pages 2–3, abstract and Methods, trial design/blinding","evidence_summary":"The trial was explicitly open label, and the report states that patients were aware of treatment-group assignment.","rationale":"Participants knew whether they received empagliflozin in addition to standard care.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.2","agent_response":"Y","evidence_location":"Page 3, Methods, “Randomization, Allocation Concealment, and Blinding”","evidence_summary":"Health care personnel and clinicians were aware of treatment-group assignment.","rationale":"Carers and intervention providers were unblinded.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.3","agent_response":"PN","evidence_location":"Pages 3–5, Methods, “Interventions and Procedures”; Results, “Trial Population and Interventions”; Table 3","evidence_summary":"The protocol specified only the addition of empagliflozin, while other perioperative care was routine. One intervention participant stopped empagliflozin because of a skin reaction, and nine procedures were changed to off-pump CABG because of intraoperative technical decisions. No control participant received an SGLT2 inhibitor before surgery.","rationale":"Reported departures were attributable to an adverse effect or clinical technical decisions rather than to the open-label trial context. No systematic trial-context-induced deviation is evident, though unblinded care leaves some residual uncertainty.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.4","agent_response":"NA","evidence_location":"Pages 3–5, intervention and trial-population descriptions","evidence_summary":"No important deviation caused by the trial context was identified.","rationale":"This question is not applicable because the preceding assessment did not identify trial-context-induced deviations requiring evaluation.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.5","agent_response":"NA","evidence_location":"Pages 3–5, intervention and trial-population descriptions","evidence_summary":"No important deviation caused by the trial context was identified.","rationale":"There are no identified trial-context-induced deviations for which balance between groups needs to be assessed.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.6","agent_response":"N","evidence_location":"Page 4, Methods, “Statistical Analysis”; Results, “Trial Population and Interventions”","evidence_summary":"The analysis was modified intention-to-treat and excluded nine randomized participants who did not undergo the planned surgery: 5 of 76 assigned to empagliflozin and 4 of 78 assigned to control. The primary analysis therefore included 71 and 74 participants, respectively.","rationale":"For an effect-of-assignment estimand, all randomized participants should generally remain in their assigned groups. Postrandomization exclusion based on whether surgery occurred is not a full intention-to-treat analysis.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.7","agent_response":"PN","evidence_location":"Page 4, Results, “Trial Population and Interventions”; Table 2","evidence_summary":"Nine of 154 randomized participants were excluded, with similar numbers in the empagliflozin and control groups. The analyzed groups contained 71 and 74 participants, and the observed AKI difference was 16 versus 29 events.","rationale":"The exclusions were few and nearly balanced, and postoperative AKI is not meaningfully assessable without surgery. Their exclusion is therefore unlikely to materially change the large event-count difference, although their outcomes and reasons for not undergoing surgery are not fully reported.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D3","question_id":"3.1","agent_response":"PY","evidence_location":"Pages 4 and 8, Results, “Trial Population and Interventions”; “Study Strengths and Limitations”; Table 2","evidence_summary":"The primary outcome is reported for all 145 participants included in the modified intention-to-treat surgical population, with denominators of 71 and 74. The authors report no loss to follow-up within 30 days, and creatinine values were available for more than 95% of participants from randomization through postoperative day 3.","rationale":"Outcome classification appears available for all or nearly all participants in the relevant surgical analysis population. The nine randomized participants who did not undergo surgery are addressed as a postrandomization analysis exclusion in Domain 2 rather than ordinary missing postoperative outcome data.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D3","question_id":"3.2","agent_response":"NA","evidence_location":"Pages 4 and 8, Results and study limitations","evidence_summary":"The target outcome was reported for essentially the full surgical analysis population.","rationale":"Further assessment of bias from missing outcome data is not required after judging that data were available for all or nearly all relevant participants.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D3","question_id":"3.3","agent_response":"NA","evidence_location":"Pages 4 and 8, Results and study limitations","evidence_summary":"No material missing postoperative AKI classifications were reported in the surgical analysis population.","rationale":"There is no material outcome-data missingness for which dependence on the true outcome value needs to be evaluated.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D3","question_id":"3.4","agent_response":"NA","evidence_location":"Pages 4 and 8, Results and study limitations","evidence_summary":"No material missing postoperative AKI classifications were reported in the surgical analysis population.","rationale":"Assessment of whether missingness likely depended on the true value is not applicable in the absence of material missing outcome data.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D4","question_id":"4.1","agent_response":"N","evidence_location":"Page 3, Methods, “Study Outcomes”; page 8, “Study Strengths and Limitations”","evidence_summary":"AKI within seven days was defined using creatinine-based stage 1 or higher criteria from KDIGO, AKIN, or RIFLE. Baseline was the most recent preoperative creatinine. The authors acknowledge that urine output was not used after the first postoperative day.","rationale":"Serum-creatinine criteria are objective, recognized methods for identifying AKI. Omitting urine output may reduce sensitivity but does not make the creatinine-based measurement inappropriate for this prespecified result.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D4","question_id":"4.2","agent_response":"PN","evidence_location":"Page 3, Methods, “Interventions and Procedures” and “Study Outcomes”; page 4, outcome availability","evidence_summary":"Serum creatinine was expected to be measured daily during ICU admission and as clinically indicated thereafter. The same definitions and blinded adjudication process were used for both groups, and creatinine availability exceeded 95% through postoperative day 3.","rationale":"The objective laboratory method and common adjudication process make differential measurement unlikely. Some uncertainty remains because measurements after ICU discharge were clinically indicated and treating clinicians were unblinded.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D4","question_id":"4.3","agent_response":"N","evidence_location":"Page 3, Methods, “Study Outcomes”","evidence_summary":"The primary AKI outcome was assessed for each criterion by an independent committee of three physicians unaware of randomized treatment assignment.","rationale":"The assessors adjudicating the target outcome were blinded to intervention assignment.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D4","question_id":"4.4","agent_response":"NA","evidence_location":"Page 3, Methods, “Study Outcomes”","evidence_summary":"Independent outcome adjudicators were unaware of randomized treatment assignment.","rationale":"Because adjudicators did not know treatment assignment, the potential influence of assessor knowledge does not apply.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D4","question_id":"4.5","agent_response":"NA","evidence_location":"Page 3, Methods, “Study Outcomes”","evidence_summary":"Independent outcome adjudicators were unaware of randomized treatment assignment.","rationale":"There was no assessor knowledge of assignment that could have influenced outcome assessment.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D5","question_id":"5.1","agent_response":"NI","evidence_location":"Pages 2–4, trial registration and Methods, “Study Outcomes” and “Statistical Analysis”","evidence_summary":"The article cites ClinicalTrials.gov registration NCT04523064, describes AKI within seven days as the primary outcome, and presents a specified unadjusted modified intention-to-treat analysis. It does not provide the registration history, dated protocol, or dated statistical analysis plan within the supplied PDF.","rationale":"The report indicates that the outcome and analysis were planned, but the supplied information does not establish that the complete analysis plan was finalized before unblinded outcome data became available.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D5","question_id":"5.2","agent_response":"PN","evidence_location":"Pages 3–4, Methods, “Study Outcomes”; page 7, Table 2","evidence_summary":"The primary outcome was explicitly defined as meeting at least one stage 1 criterion under KDIGO, AKIN, or RIFLE within seven days. Table 2 reports the prespecified composite and its component definitions.","rationale":"Although several AKI definitions were measured, the article identifies the composite as the primary measurement and reports the component results, making selective choice among measurements unlikely.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D5","question_id":"5.3","agent_response":"PN","evidence_location":"Page 4, Methods, “Statistical Analysis”; pages 4 and 7, Results and Table 2","evidence_summary":"The reported primary result is the specified unadjusted relative risk in the modified intention-to-treat population. Per-protocol and alternative-baseline sensitivity analyses are described as producing similar findings.","rationale":"There were potentially multiple analytical approaches, but the report distinguishes the primary analysis from sensitivity analyses and does not suggest that the favorable estimate was selected from competing eligible analyses. Lack of a dated accessible analysis plan prevents a definitive no.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"}],"domain_assessments":[{"domain_id":"D1","provisional_domain_judgement":"Low","domain_rationale":"The automated, stratified, variable-block randomization process was appropriate, allocation was probably concealed through the electronic system, and baseline differences did not indicate a randomization problem."},{"domain_id":"D2","provisional_domain_judgement":"Some concerns","domain_rationale":"The trial was open label, but no important trial-context-induced deviations were identified and outcome adjudication was blinded. However, nine participants were excluded after randomization because they did not undergo surgery, so the analysis was not a full effect-of-assignment analysis. The small, nearly balanced exclusions are unlikely to have materially changed the result."},{"domain_id":"D3","provisional_domain_judgement":"Low","domain_rationale":"AKI outcomes were reported for essentially all participants in the relevant surgical analysis population, with no reported loss to follow-up. The separate postrandomization exclusion of participants who did not undergo surgery is considered under Domain 2."},{"domain_id":"D4","provisional_domain_judgement":"Low","domain_rationale":"AKI was measured using objective, recognized serum-creatinine criteria and adjudicated by an independent committee blinded to assignment. Lack of urine-output criteria may reduce detection but was common to both groups and does not indicate differential measurement bias."},{"domain_id":"D5","provisional_domain_judgement":"Some concerns","domain_rationale":"The primary outcome and principal analysis are clearly identified, and reporting of component and sensitivity analyses makes selective reporting unlikely. Nevertheless, the supplied PDF does not establish through a dated protocol, registration history, or statistical analysis plan that the complete analysis plan was finalized before unblinded data were available."}],"agent_overall_provisional_judgement":"Some concerns","agent_overall_rationale":"The result has low risk of bias from randomization, missing outcome data, and outcome measurement. The main concerns are the postrandomization modified intention-to-treat exclusions and the inability to verify from the supplied material that the full analysis plan was finalized before unblinded outcome data were available. Neither issue alone appears likely to create major bias, so a High judgement is not warranted."}
